sections.h2: Selling a house in New Windsor
sections.html:
New Windsor is a town in eastern Orange County, on the Hudson's west shore directly below the city of Newburgh. It is a patchwork of hamlets rather than one village: Vails Gate, Rock Tavern, Little Britain, Beaver Dam Lake and Firthcliffe Heights. Rock Tavern and Vails Gate each have their own ZIP code.

Population is 27,844, almost unchanged since 2020, so you are selling into a settled suburb. Owners live in 73.2 percent of homes. The median home value is $371,900 and typical rent is $1,606. There are 10,981 households, and the average commute is 37.3 minutes one way, which fits a town whose main road links are the Thruway and state routes.

Older neighborhoods keep traces of the town's past. Clancyville, also called Ducktown, grew in the late 1800s around mills on Quassaick Creek, and the families who built small homes there enlarged them over generations. Those additions are a common source of permit questions, so pull your paperwork before you list.

Anyone selling a very old farmhouse, including one of the stone houses from the 1700s near Little Britain, should ask the town building department about historic or zoning limits before planning repairs. The climate brings four distinct seasons, so roof condition and heating systems deserve attention in your walk-through.

Four districts reach into the town: Newburgh City, Washingtonville Central, Cornwall Central and Valley Central, which is based in Montgomery. The answer depends on the street, so check by address instead of assuming. The district also determines the school tax bill a new owner receives.

Write the district name for your house into the paperwork you give the buyer, so nobody has to guess later.

Property tax bills are mailed in the last week of December and carry no penalty if paid in January. After that the Receiver of Taxes applies the charges below, and bills still unpaid after April 1 go to the county.

New Windsor late payment charges
Payment monthCharge from the Town of New Windsor
JanuaryNo penalty
February1 percent
MarchAnother 1 percent, plus a $2.00 notice fee
After April 1Unpaid bills go to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance

A USPS postmark now shows the day mail is processed, which can be later than the day it is dropped off, and a postage-meter mark does not count. To make sure a payment counts as on time, use one of these:

  • Ask for a hand-stamped postmark at the Post Office counter
  • Mail the check well before the due date
  • Pay in person at the Receiver of Taxes office
  • Pay online by e-check

If a bank holds your escrow, the bill goes to the bank. Anyone who refinanced or paid off a loan should tell the Receiver so the next bill reaches the right person.

The Assessor deals with exemptions, and the Building Department deals with permits. Owners who age into Enhanced STAR, or who have an ownership change, no longer file with the assessor. The state tells local assessors instead, and an ownership change is reported through the Homeowner Benefit Portal at the NYS Tax Department.

The Building Department enforces the New York State Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code and the town's zoning law. Its permit list covers building permits, decks, pools and backflow preventers. If you added a deck or pool, ask for the permit and inspection record before you list.

The Orange County Clerk records the deed. A copy of your deed costs about $5 straight from the office, and a free alert service notifies you when a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name, a guard against deed fraud. The TP-584 return goes to the county clerk, with payment due within 15 days of the deed's delivery.

sections.h2: Getting ready for a quick sale
sections.html: Start with the three offices that touch your house. Ask the Receiver of Taxes for the current balance, the Building Department for permit and inspection records, and the Orange County Clerk for a copy of your deed. Next, find your payoff figure. With those in hand, a buyer's attorney can move straight to a contract. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and repair demands, so the closing date is mostly set by title work and your own schedule.

faqs.q: Is New Windsor a town or a city?
faqs.a: A town in Orange County. The separate city of Newburgh runs along part of its northern line, and the Newburgh City School District covers sections of New Windsor.

faqs.q: What does a late New Windsor tax payment cost?
faqs.a: One percent in February, then a further one percent and a $2.00 notice fee in March. After April 1, unpaid bills go to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance.

faqs.q: How many school districts serve New Windsor?
faqs.a: Four: Newburgh, Washingtonville, Cornwall and Valley Central. Your address decides which one applies.

faqs.q: Who records a New Windsor deed?
faqs.a: The Orange County Clerk, not Town Hall. The TP-584 transfer tax form goes with the deed, and payment is due within 15 days after delivery.

faqs.q: What is the state transfer tax on a New Windsor home?
faqs.a: Two dollars per $500 of the price, charged to the seller unless the contract shifts it. The buyer's 1 percent mansion tax starts only at $1 million.
